subject.title: fix(cron): emit scheduled events after durable wake changes

question: Should `scheduled` become a permanent public `cron_changed` action with best-effort, unordered reconciliation semantics?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound, but adding a discriminant to the shipped plugin API fixes a permanent external contract that automation should not choose.

options.title: Approve additive action
options.body: Accept `scheduled` as the canonical post-commit hint and retain the documented debounce, full-list reconciliation, and gateway-start recovery guidance.

options.title: Keep polling-only contract
options.body: Decline the action expansion and revise the existing docs so external schedulers rely on startup and full-list polling instead.

recommendation.title: Approve additive action
recommendation.body: Accept `scheduled` as the canonical post-commit hint and retain the documented debounce, full-list reconciliation, and gateway-start recovery guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns most of the recent cron persistence and Gateway history and is the strongest available contract decision owner.
